post.description: Answer what gear a WoW Forever character should wear or aim for at its level: pass class, spec, level and mode. Chain an item id into `item` for its full stats and sources.

level.description:
Character level, 1-60. Default: the beta level cap (30). Items above the cap are labelled Speculation by the site.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 60.

mode.description:
pve (default, raid stat weights), pvp, or leveling (ForeverDB's leveling weights: more Stamina and armor).

Provider reference: allowed values ["pve", "pvp", "leveling"].

spec.description:
Spec slug of that class: druid balance/feral/restoration, hunter beast-mastery/marksmanship/survival, mage arcane/fire/frost, paladin holy/protection/retribution, priest discipline/holy/shadow, rogue assassination/combat/subtlety, shaman elemental/enhancement/restoration, warlock affliction/demonology/destruction, warrior arms/fury/protection.

Provider reference: allowed values ["balance", "feral", "restoration", "beast-mastery", "marksmanship", "survival", "arcane", "fire", "frost", "holy", "protection", "retribution", "discipline", "shadow", "assassination", "combat", "subtlety", "elemental", "enhancement", "affliction", "demonology", "destruction", "arms", "fury"].

post.description: Answer what talents a WoW Forever character should take: pass class, and spec and level when known. With level, only the builds for the highest build level at or below it are returned (a level 25 character gets the level 20 builds); below 20 the list is empty.

level.description:
Character level, 1-60: keeps the builds for the highest build level at or below it.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 60.

spec.description:

builds.how_to_play: Charge in, use Bloodrage, and keep Battle Shout up. Between Charge and Anger Management's trickle you rarely start a fight with an empty bar, so you can Rend straight away on anything that will live a while. Press Overpower every time the target dodges and put spare Rage into Heroic Strike. You learn Slam and Cleave at 20: Slam hits hard, but its 1.5 sec cast delays your next swing, so start it right after a swing lands. If a pull goes wrong, Tactical Mastery (level 14) keeps up to 10 Rage when you drop into Defensive Stance, and Improved Tactical Mastery keeps up to 15 more.
builds.name: Two-hander leveling with Anger Management
builds.summary: A two-handed leveling build that heads straight for Anger Management, which in Forever generates Rage in combat as well as slowing Rage loss. Improved Heroic Strike at 3/3 takes 3 Rage off your Rage dump, and 2 points of Deflection add a little parry.

talents.name: Improved Heroic Strike
talents.reason: Rank 3 cuts Heroic Strike's cost by 3 Rage (1 per rank), and Heroic Strike is where most of your spare Rage goes, so the saving adds up over every fight.

talents.name: Deflection
talents.reason: Rank 2 adds 2% Parry chance (1% per rank); every parry is a hit you don't take while you solo, and these 2 points complete the 5 tier 1 points that open tier 2.

talents.name: Improved Tactical Mastery
talents.reason: At 5/5 Tactical Mastery keeps up to an additional 15 Rage when you change stances, so a switch to Defensive Stance on a bad pull costs you little; 5 points here are required for Anger Management.

talents.name: Anger Management
talents.reason: Generates 1 Rage every 3 sec in combat and reduces Rage loss out of combat by 30%, so you start and finish fights with Rage to spend.

builds.how_to_play: Let the tank get a few hits in first; Heroic Strike causes a high amount of threat, so hold it until the tank has a lead. Rend the tank's target on anything bigger than a trash mob, Overpower whenever it dodges, and Slam right after a swing when Slam is off cooldown. When two enemies stand together and nothing crowd-controlled is nearby, use Cleave instead of Heroic Strike. Anger Management keeps Rage coming even when you aren't taking hits, which is exactly the situation in a group.
builds.name: Anger Management with Improved Rend
builds.summary: For dungeon runs at 20: the same Anger Management core, but with 3 points in Improved Rend, which makes Rend's bleed 35% stronger, since enemies live longer when someone else tanks. Those 3 points also unlock Deep Wounds for your next point at level 21.

talents.name: Improved Rend
talents.reason: Rank 3 adds 35% to Rend's bleed damage (12% at rank 1, 23% at rank 2), and 3 points here unlock Deep Wounds.

talents.name: Improved Heroic Strike
talents.reason: Rank 2 cuts Heroic Strike's cost by 2 Rage, and with Improved Rend's 3 points it makes the 5 tier 1 points that open tier 2.

talents.name: Improved Tactical Mastery
talents.reason: At 5/5 Tactical Mastery keeps up to an additional 15 Rage when you change stances, so a switch to Defensive Stance on a bad pull costs you little; 5 points here are required for Anger Management.

talents.name: Anger Management
talents.reason: Generates 1 Rage every 3 sec in combat and reduces Rage loss out of combat by 30%, so you start and finish fights with Rage to spend.

builds.how_to_play: Open with Charge while you are still out of combat, then Hamstring at once so the target can't walk out of melee range. Use Bloodrage after Charge, never before: it puts you in combat, and Charge can't be used in combat. Rend the target, press Overpower whenever they dodge, and spend spare Rage on Heroic Strike. Slam has a cast time, so use it only when the target stands and fights you. Disarm needs Defensive Stance: use it on Rogues, Warriors, Paladins and Shamans when they start hitting hard. Against several melee players, Thunder Clap makes them attack slower and Retaliation punishes every hit they land from the front. When you are losing, change to Defensive Stance; Tactical Mastery and Improved Tactical Mastery mean you keep Rage when you do.
builds.name: Deflection and Anger Management for PvP
builds.summary: A level 20 PvP build that spends on Rage and survival instead of Improved Rend. Five points of Deflection add 5% parry against melee classes, and Anger Management keeps Rage coming while casters and Hunters keep you at range. Compared with the dungeon build you give up Improved Rend and the path to Deep Wounds, which pay off on long fights against a target that stands still, not against players who move and heal. Improved Charge and Improved Overpower come at 30.

talents.name: Deflection
talents.reason: At 5/5 you parry 5% more often (1% per rank). Rogues, Warriors, Paladins and Shamans all fight you in melee, every parried swing is damage you don't take, and 5 points here open tier 2.

talents.name: Improved Tactical Mastery
talents.reason: At 5/5 Tactical Mastery keeps up to an additional 15 Rage when you change stances, so you can drop into Defensive Stance under pressure and come back without an empty bar; 5 points here are required for Anger Management.

talents.name: Anger Management
talents.reason: Generates 1 Rage every 3 sec while in combat, so you still build Rage while a Mage or Hunter keeps you from hitting them, and reduces Rage loss out of combat by 30%, so you often start the next fight with Rage left.
